public_rationale: The plain reading is that OpenAI had no workable compute source outside Microsoft when the post ran. On March 10, 2025, OpenAI signed a CoreWeave deal worth up to $11.9B. In the same release Sam Altman described CoreWeave as complementing "our commercial deals with Microsoft and Oracle" and the Stargate joint venture (e1). Oracle infrastructure had been providing capacity for OpenAI since a June 2024 agreement, though it was framed as an extension of Azure (e2). Reuters later reported that OpenAI relied on Oracle and CoreWeave as well as Microsoft and finalized a Google Cloud deal in May 2025 (e3). In fairness, Azure was OpenAI's exclusive provider until January 2025, and the claim may mean that no non-Microsoft option was big enough. But the post's own text names CoreWeave as a real choice, and OpenAI had named non-Microsoft deals before the post.
limitations: 'Viable' is subjective. If it means capacity big enough to meet all of OpenAI's growth at once, the claim is harder to test.
How much compute non-Microsoft providers actually delivered in early 2025 is not public.
